headline: Senate Panel Backs Bill Setting 16 as Minimum Age for Social Media
seoTitle: Senate Panel Backs Social Media Minimum Age of 16 | FMB News
seoDescription: A Philippine Senate panel endorsed a bill that would set 16 as the minimum age for social media accounts and require privacy-compliant age assurance.
deck: The proposed Child Online Safety and Protection Act would require platforms to prevent children below 16 from creating or maintaining accounts through privacy-compliant age-assurance systems.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Senate committee on public information and mass media endorsed Senate Bill No. 2424, or the proposed Child Online Safety and Protection Act, to the Senate floor on August 26.

The measure would set 16 as the minimum age for social media use and require platforms to use reasonable and effective age-assurance systems to prevent children below that age from creating or maintaining accounts.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The proposal distinguishes age assurance, which may assess user behavior and other technical signals, from age-verification systems that typically require identification documents. Any age-assurance system would have to comply with the Data Privacy Act.

The bill would also restrict the commercial use of children's personal information. Committee chair Sen. Robinhood Padilla said the proposal seeks to reduce online risks while acknowledging that experts differ on the appropriate minimum age.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: If enacted, the measure would place new child-safety and privacy obligations on social media platforms. It would not create an immediate nationwide social media ban, and the proposed restrictions are not yet law.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The bill remains subject to Senate deliberation and possible amendment. It would still need approval by both chambers of Congress and the President before taking effect.
